title: GMAT exam hub on mba.com
why: The official place to register, read policies, check fees and find free prep.
when: All phases; essential in Test & Apply

title: mba.com
why: Your account, scores, score sending and the official store all live here.

title: GMAC
why: The exam owner's news and announcements, including Superscore and concordance updates.

title: GMAT Official Starter Kit and Practice Exams 1 and 2
why: Real sample questions and two full-length adaptive exams with the real scoring.

title: GMAT Official Guide 2026-2027
why: Over 975 real questions with explanations, the best realistic practice available.

title: Official Guide Quant, Verbal and Data Insights Reviews
why: Extra official questions in one area, useful once you know your weakest section.

title: GMAT Official Practice Questions
cost: Paid (approx US$30 per section, about US$80 for the bundle)
why: Section-specific sets of real questions for targeted practice.

title: GMAT Official Practice Exams 3 to 6
cost: Paid (approx US$108-110 for all four; check mba.com)
why: The best predictor of your real score, with the real algorithm and timing.

title: Wiley (publisher of the Official Guide)
cost: Paid (approx US$43 for the Official Guide)
why: An alternative place to buy the Official Guide in print or as an e-book.

title: Pearson VUE
why: Test centre information; confirm Delhi NCR locations and what to expect on the day.

title: GMAT Club forum
why: The largest GMAT community with explanations, study plans and score stories.

title: GMAT Club
cost: Free (mocks paid, approx US$100 for 3 months)
why: Question bank, tests, study plans and school information in one place.

title: Beat The GMAT
why: Forums and success stories, helpful for morale and recent test-day reports.

title: r/GMAT on Reddit
why: Quick questions, recent test-day experiences and motivation from other test-takers.

title: Khan Academy maths
why: Rebuild school-level arithmetic and algebra from the ground up.

title: YouTube
why: Free lessons from several prep providers; prefer recent videos on the current exam.

title: Target Test Prep
cost: Paid (reports vary, roughly US$150-250 a month; check site)
why: Deep, structured Quant course with a large question bank and error tracking.

title: e-GMAT
cost: Paid (reported roughly US$300-400; free trial available)
why: Strong on Critical Reasoning, Reading Comprehension and Data Insights, with adaptive tools.

title: Manhattan Prep
why: Well-regarded teaching and live courses, the most expensive option here.

title: Magoosh GMAT
cost: Paid (plans listed about US$199 for 6 months; check site)
why: Friendly video lessons and a free trial; a gentle, affordable choice.

title: Experts' Global
cost: Paid (mocks reported about US$90 for 6 months; one mock free)
why: Budget-friendly Indian provider with many full-length mocks.

title: GMAT Ninja
why: Excellent concept explanations; check that older content still applies to the current exam.

title: CrackVerbal
why: India-based coaching with free guides, including a Data Sufficiency guide.

title: The Economist
why: Dense, well-organised argument, ideal for building a Reading Comprehension habit.

title: Aeon
why: Long essays on ideas and culture that train you on abstract, idea-heavy writing.

title: Scientific American
why: Clear science writing, close to the style of RC science passages.

title: Smithsonian Magazine
why: History and science in accessible prose, good for relaxed reading practice.

title: The Atlantic
why: Long-form essays on society and ideas for stamina and argument-tracking.

title: Harvard Business Review
why: Business reasoning close to Critical Reasoning and Data Insights content.

title: Our World in Data
why: Real charts and datasets to practise reading graphs and tables.

title: Gapminder
why: Interactive charts that build data-reading intuition for Data Insights.

title: Anki
cost: Free on desktop and Android; paid on iPhone
why: Optional spaced-repetition flashcards if you want a second tool beyond the app.

title: Indian School of Business
why: Official ISB admissions pages, class profile and policies for your target programme.

title: Roediger and Karpicke (2006) on PubMed
why: The original test-enhanced learning study behind retrieval practice.

title: Cepeda et al. (2006) on PubMed
why: The review of distributed practice research behind spaced study.
